prompt.context: Our client, So Fresh and So Clean, is a cleaning supply distributor and operates a national distribution network. Over the past 5 years the client has acquired several small regional players and has experienced decreasing margins. In 2009, the company's net margin was 3.1% and since the net margin has dwindled to 2.4% at the end of 2013. The CEO is worried about long-term longevity of the company and hired us to conduct an extensive diagnostic of the company's health.
prompt.question: How would you approach this problem?

clarifying_info.q: What products does the client sell and who are their customers?
clarifying_info.a: The client provides chemicals, cleaning supplies, uniforms, and equipment to restaurants, hospitals, schools, and other food service providers. Located within the United States.

clarifying_info.q: How has the overall market been growing?
clarifying_info.a: The market has averaged 2% growth over the past five years.

clarifying_info.q: What is the client's market position relative to competitors?
clarifying_info.a: So Fresh and So Clean is the industry leader with 20% market share, followed by competitor A at 15%, B at 8%, C at 5%, and others make up the rest.

clarifying_info.q: What acquisitions has the company made?
clarifying_info.a: The company acquired a $3.3B revenue competitor in 2010 and a $3.1B revenue competitor in 2012.

exhibits.title: Market analysis and competitor benchmark
exhibits.shows: Cleaning supply distribution market size in USD billions over time alongside a net margin industry benchmark comparison
exhibits.data: Market size trend over multiple years; net margin benchmarks for So Fresh and So Clean vs. industry competitors

exhibits.title: 5 Year Financial Performance (2009-2013)
exhibits.shows: Income statement line items for So Fresh and So Clean from 2009 to 2013 with year-over-year percentage changes

exhibits.title: Breakdown of typical sales person monthly activity in 2013
exhibits.shows: Breakdown of how sales representatives at So Fresh and So Clean vs. competitors allocate their time across different activities each month
exhibits.data: Comparison of time spent selling vs. administrative and other tasks between So Fresh and So Clean reps and competitor reps

framework: Assess market health: Is the overall market growing or declining? How does client profitability compare to the industry benchmark?
Analyze internal profitability via a P&L tree: revenue, COGS, gross profit, operating expenses
Identify the cost driver: examine SG&A and operating expense trends, especially around acquisition years 2010 and 2012
Diagnose root cause: investigate why SG&A has increased disproportionately — focus on salesforce efficiency post-acquisition
Quantify the fix: model cost savings from a restructured salesforce with account coordinators
Develop recommendation: weigh benefits vs. risks of the new selling model

questions.prompt: After reviewing Exhibit 1, what does the market analysis tell you and how should the investigation proceed?
questions.guidance: Strong candidates recognize the market is mature (2% growth) and that So Fresh and So Clean's profitability is broadly in line with the industry benchmark. This means the problem is unlikely to be market-driven and the focus should shift to internal operations. The candidate should pivot to a profitability tree.

questions.prompt: After reviewing Exhibit 2, what do you observe about the 5-year financial performance?
questions.guidance: Gross profit margins have been stable (~18%), so the problem is not in cost of goods sold. The key insight is that SG&A jumped 58% in 2010 and another 55% in 2012 (both acquisition years), growing from $0.60B to $1.60B. This disproportionate SG&A increase while sales grew only 19% and 13% in those years is the primary driver of margin compression. The candidate should brainstorm ways to lower sales costs (reductions, organizational restructuring, technology).

math.setup: Compare SG&A as a percentage of sales in 2009 vs. 2013 to show the structural cost increase.
steps: SG&A absolute increase: $1.60B - $0.60B = $1.00B (167% rise over 5 years)
Net earnings barely moved: $0.58B (2009) to $0.63B (2013) despite revenue growing from $18.79B to $26.39B
math.answer: SG&A nearly doubled as a share of revenue, absorbing acquisition gains and compressing net margin from 3.1% to 2.4%.

questions.prompt: Based on Exhibit 3, what do you observe about how sales reps spend their time, and what would you recommend?
questions.guidance: Competitors spend approximately 2x the amount of time selling compared to So Fresh and So Clean reps, who spend a disproportionate share of time on administrative tasks. The candidate should identify this gap and brainstorm ways to increase selling time: hire entry-level account coordinators for admin tasks, invest in CRM/technology, restructure territories, create shared service centers for admin functions, provide rep training on time management.

questions.prompt: Under the new model, the client would hire 148 entry-level account coordinators at $55K salary to handle administrative tasks, freeing sales reps from processing 16 orders per week (each taking 25 minutes). There are 1,500 sales reps earning $120,000 per year working 40-hour weeks. How much would this model save per year?
questions.guidance: The candidate must calculate net saving: investment cost of new coordinators minus the productivity-equivalent savings from reduced rep time on admin. A strong candidate correctly converts time saved into a fraction of rep salary.

math.setup: Net saving = Benefit (fraction of rep time freed x total rep compensation) - Investment (cost of new coordinators).
steps: Investment: 148 account coordinators x $55,000 = $8,140,000 (casebook rounds to ~150 x $55,000 = $8,250,000)
Time saved per rep per week: 16 orders x 25 minutes = 400 minutes
Total working minutes per week: 40 hours x 60 minutes = 2,400 minutes
math.answer: Net annual saving of approximately $21.75M, representing a ~2.1% improvement to 2013 operating income.

brainstorming.prompt: What are specific ways to lower sales costs or increase the percentage of time sales representatives spend actually selling?

categories.name: Workforce restructuring
ideas: Hire entry-level account coordinators to handle administrative tasks
Rationalize overlapping salesforce territories from acquisitions
Reduce total headcount through attrition where territories overlap
Create tiered sales roles such as hunter vs. farmer

categories.name: Technology and automation
ideas: Implement a CRM system to automate order entry and tracking
Deploy mobile tools for reps to process orders in the field
Use electronic data interchange with large customers to eliminate manual orders

categories.name: Organizational design
ideas: Create a shared services center for administrative functions
Centralize customer service to handle routine inquiries off reps' plates
Restructure reporting lines post-acquisition to eliminate redundancy

categories.name: Sales process improvement
ideas: Redesign sales territories to minimize non-selling travel time
Focus reps on high-value accounts and use inside sales for smaller accounts
Introduce account segmentation to allocate rep time by customer value
Set minimum selling-time targets with manager oversight

recommendation: So Fresh and So Clean's margin decline is driven by a bloated under-rationalized salesforce following its 2010 and 2012 acquisitions — SG&A nearly doubled as a share of revenue while gross margins held flat

Implement a new selling model by hiring approximately 148 account coordinators at $55K each to absorb administrative tasks, freeing 1/6 of each sales rep's time and delivering approximately $21.75M in net annual savings
Longer term, rationalize the combined salesforce, invest in CRM and automation, and standardize processes across acquired entities to structurally reduce SG&A back toward the 3-4% of sales baseline
risks: A 17% reduction in effective salesforce capacity could reduce customer coverage and service levels, potentially causing churn
Change management risk: sales reps may resist the new model or account coordinator roles
$21.75M savings is small relative to the enterprise scale — additional levers such as further headcount reduction and technology investment are needed to materially restore margins
Integration of three companies' cultures and systems may be slow and costly
next_steps: Design the account coordinator role and onboarding program
Pilot the new model in one region before national rollout
Quantify the full salesforce rationalization opportunity from headcount overlap across acquisitions
Assess technology investment required for CRM and order automation
Set a target SG&A as percentage of sales and build a roadmap to achieve it
